mainText:
If you only remember one thing. Three fired Open A I safety researchers went public. They say the firings chill the company's safety culture.

Section one. A I safety.

From your Rundown. Three researchers fired by Open A I, Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang, and Mikita Balesni, published an open letter. They deny mishandling sensitive information. They say they acted within their jobs. They warn the firings could give Open A I cover to skip embedding outside auditors. Open A I agrees with their recommendations, but says the firings were not about raising concerns, and cites a pattern of misconduct.

Also from your Rundown. Anthropic updated its usage policy. Starting November twelfth, users can't subject Claude to sustained, needless abuse. It's the first rule aimed at protecting the A I itself. Microsoft A I's Mustafa Suleyman disagrees with the approach.

Why it matters. Safety promises now depend on who gets to check the work.

Section two. Models and agents.

From your Rundown. A wave of personal A I agents has launched in recent weeks. Meta's Muse, Open A I's Dots, Grok Bot, and Hark Pro. Google's new Gemini four Argon is challenging the top models. Anthropic released Haiku five point five, a budget model, plus Claude Dashboards and Motion. Anthropic also launched a free scanner that uses its strongest models to find vulnerabilities in open source code.

Why it matters. The race is shifting from chatbots to agents that work for you all day.

Section three. Politics and policy.

From your Rundown, citing Axios. President Trump called people who refuse to say Super Intelligence instead of A I, quote, the enemy. This follows an executive order directing federal agencies to use the term.

Why it matters. Words come first, rules come later. That is a messaging story for your world.

Section four. A I and science.

From your Information weekend newsletter. Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan's Biohub announced a one point eight billion dollar partnership with the N I H and the Department of Energy, for what they call A I powered biology. Meta, Google DeepMind, and Isomorphic Labs add three hundred million dollars. Anthropic also expanded its government partnership, with one hundred fifty million dollars of A I credits for the Genesis Mission. The Information notes that science is shifting from universities to big tech. Of thirteen members on the president's science council, only one is an academic researcher.

Also from your Rundown. An independent researcher used Claude Code and Codex to spot a possible new planet in old NASA telescope data.

Why it matters. Big tech is becoming the main funder of science.

Section five. Tech for good.

From Fortune. The International Rescue Committee's Jeannie Annan says aid groups should embrace A I and scrutinize it. About two hundred sixty million people need help, and aid is down twenty five percent since twenty twenty four. Their Signpost assistant improved from fifty two to seventy seven percent on tests. It still fails about one answer in four. So humans review every answer.

Also, a teacher used A I to revive a fifteen year old school Minecraft world, still growing with student projects.

Why it matters. Good A I use means evidence, human oversight, and published failures.

Also in your Reads. The New Yorker looks at the Elizabeth Holmes documentary, and at a shooting by immigration agents in New York. Noosphere has filmmaker Alex Gibney calling Elon Musk an investor, not an inventor. Your Information also covers techies hoarding A I computers at home.

The thread today. Who checks the A I, and who funds the science.
